Implemented the fix in django/db/models/sql/query.py (the only allowed file).

Change: In `Query.get_aggregation`, added a `has_window` check that detects whether any annotation contains a window function (`contains_over_clause`), and added it to the condition that decides whether to wrap the query in an inner subquery. When window functions are present, the aggregation is now computed in an outer `AggregateQuery` over an inner subquery that computes the window function, so the generated SQL no longer nests an aggregate over a window function (fixing "aggregate function calls cannot contain window function calls" / "misuse of window function").

Verification: scoped_tests public regression selection (`aggregation`) passed — 124 tests, OK, returncode 0, with the edit on disk (code_revision 108b14ff...). Host feature acceptance runs separately.
